_note: New York advance-notice requirement for rent increases / non-renewal (HSTPA 2019), retrieved verbatim from nysenate.gov on 2026-06-17. RPL § 226-c: where a landlord will not renew or will raise rent by 5% or more, written notice is required — 30 days (occupancy/lease under 1 year), 60 days (1 to under 2 years), 90 days (2 years or more). status=draft-unverified.

rules.title: Rent increase or non-renewal without statutory notice
rules.description: Per RPL § 226-c, a landlord who intends to raise rent by 5% or more, or not to renew, must give advance written notice scaled to how long the tenant has lived there: 30 days (under 1 year), 60 days (1 to under 2 years), or 90 days (2 years or more). A clause letting the landlord raise rent 'at any time' or on shorter notice conflicts with this. Flag to check the notice period.
rules.tenant_explainer: Your landlord has to give you real warning before a rent hike of 5% or more — 30, 60, or 90 days depending on how long you've lived there. A clause saying rent can go up 'at any time' or with only a few days' notice doesn't match the law.

citations.label: N.Y. Real Property Law § 226-c
citations.quote: Whenever a landlord intends to offer to renew the tenancy with a rent increase equal to or greater than five percent … or the landlord does not intend to renew the tenancy, the landlord shall provide written notice … [at least] thirty days [if occupancy/lease is less than one year]; sixty days [one year or more but less than two years]; ninety days [two years or more].
